tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import re
5	
6	from .errors import MiniSQLError
7	from .formatting import format_csv, format_table
8	
9	PROMPT = "minisql> "
10	CONTINUATION = "   ...> "
11	_WS = " \t\r\n"
12	
13	HELP = (
14	    "Enter SQL statements terminated by ';'.\n"
15	    "Commands:\n"
16	    "  .help                 show this help\n"
17	    "  .tables               list tables\n"
18	    "  .schema NAME          show columns of table NAME\n"
19	    "  .format csv|table     set output format\n"
20	    "  .quit, .exit          leave the REPL\n"
21	)
22	
23	
24	def _error(stdout, stderr, text: str) -> None:
25	    stdout.flush()
26	    stderr.write(text + "\n")
27	    stderr.flush()
28	
29	
30	def _guarded(stdout, stderr, action) -> None:
31	    """Run `action()`; MiniSQLError / unexpected errors become one stderr line (D19)."""
32	    try:
33	        action()
34	    except MiniSQLError as err:
35	        _error(stdout, stderr, str(err))
36	    except Exception as exc:
37	        _error(stdout, stderr, "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: %s" % (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__))
38	
39	
40	def run_repl(conn, fmt: str, stdin, stdout, stderr) -> int:
41	    state = {"fmt": fmt}
42	    buffer = None  # None = empty buffer; otherwise the accumulated text
43	
44	    def write(text: str) -> None:
45	        stdout.write(text)
46	        stdout.flush()
47	
48	    def execute(sql: str) -> None:
49	        result = conn.execute(sql)
50	        write(format_csv(result) if state["fmt"] == "csv" else format_table(result))
51	
52	    def schema(name: str) -> None:
53	        write("".join("%s %s\n" % col for col in conn.schema(name)))
54	
55	    def command(stripped: str) -> bool:
56	        """Run a dot-command; return True when the REPL should exit."""
57	        parts = re.split(r"[ \t]+", stripped)
58	        word, args = parts[0], parts[1:]
59	        if word in (".quit", ".exit") and not args:
60	            return True
61	        if word == ".help" and not args:
62	            write(HELP)
63	        elif word == ".tables" and not args:
64	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: write("".join(t + "\n" for t in conn.tables())))
65	        elif word == ".schema" and len(args) == 1:
66	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: schema(args[0]))
67	        elif word == ".format" and len(args) == 1 and args[0] in ("csv", "table"):
68	            state["fmt"] = args[0]
69	        else:
70	            _error(stdout, stderr, "unknown command: " + stripped)
71	        return False
72	
73	    while True:
74	        write(PROMPT if buffer is None else CONTINUATION)
75	        line = stdin.readline()
76	        if line == "":
77	            if buffer is not None:
78	                _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: execute(buffer))
79	            return 0
80	        if line.endswith("\n"):
81	            line = line[:-1]
82	        if buffer is None:
83	            stripped = line.strip(_WS)
84	            if not stripped:
85	                continue
86	            if stripped.startswith("."):
87	                if command(stripped):
88	                    return 0
89	                continue
90	            buffer = line
91	        else:
92	            buffer += "\n" + line
93	        if buffer.rstrip(_WS).endswith(";"):
94	            sql, buffer = buffer, None
95	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: execute(sql))

1	# minisql: Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- Stack: Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- Package location: `minisql/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`), with `__init__.py` and `__main__.py`.
7	- Entry points: `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` from repo root; `import minisql; minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
8	- Do not use `sqlite3` or any existing SQL engine or parser.
9	
10	## Functional requirements
11	
12	- **R1** Importable as `minisql`, runnable as `python -m minisql`; standard-library imports only, never `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser.
13	- **R2** Tables load from the data directory per the data contract.
14	- **R3** Column types are inferred per the inference rules; empty fields are NULL.
15	- **R4** The tokenizer implements the lexical rules.
16	- **R5** The parser implements the grammar and precedence table.
17	- **R6** Keywords and all names resolve case-insensitively.
18	- **R7** Expressions are statically typed; violations are SemanticErrors raised before any row is evaluated.
19	- **R8** Arithmetic follows the numeric rules, including division by zero.
20	- **R9** Predicates follow three-valued logic.
21	- **R10** Projection supports `*`, `t.*`, expressions, aliases and the output naming rule.
22	- **R11** INNER and LEFT joins follow nested-loop semantics and order.
23	- **R12** Grouping, `HAVING` and aggregates follow the aggregate rules, including empty input.
24	- **R13** `DISTINCT` keeps first occurrences.
25	- **R14** `ORDER BY` supports aliases, ordinals, expressions, multiple keys, `ASC`/`DESC`; NULLs smallest; stable ties.
26	- **R15** `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take non-negative integer literals.
27	- **R16** Clauses evaluate in the defined order; `AND`/`OR` short-circuit.
28	- **R17** The library API matches the contract.
29	- **R18** CSV and table formats match byte-for-byte.
30	- **R19** The one-shot CLI follows the output and exit-code rules.
31	- **R20** The REPL follows the prompt, buffering, command and exit rules.
32	- **R21** Errors use the specified classes, format, templates and positions.
33	
34	## Language reference
35	
36	### Lexical rules
37	
38	- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
39	- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
40	- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
41	- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
42	- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
43	- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.
44	- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . * ;`.
45	
46	### Grammar (EBNF)
47	
48	```
49	query     = "SELECT" ["DISTINCT"] item {"," item}
50	            ["FROM" tableref {join}] ["WHERE" expr]
51	            ["GROUP" "BY" expr {"," expr}] ["HAVING" expr]
52	            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
53	            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;
54	item      = "*" | name "." "*" | expr [["AS"] name] ;
55	tableref  = name [["AS"] name] ;
56	join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
57	order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
58	expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
59	and       = not {"AND" not} ;
60	not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
61	cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
62	                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]
63	                | ["NOT"] "IN" "(" expr {"," expr} ")" ] ;
64	cmpop     = "=" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ;
65	add       = mul {("+" | "-") mul} ;
66	mul       = unary {("*" | "/" | "%") unary} ;
67	unary     = ("-" | "+") unary | primary ;
68	primary   = INT | REAL | STRING | "NULL" | call | colref | "(" expr ")" ;
69	call      = name "(" ("*" | expr) ")" ;
70	colref    = name ["." name] ;
71	name      = IDENT | QUOTED_IDENT ;
72	```
73	
74	`FROM` is optional; without it the query runs over exactly one empty row. A table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier in that query.
75	
76	### Precedence (highest first)
77	
78	| Level | Operators | Associativity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
81	| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
82	| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
83	| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
84	| 5 | `NOT` | right |
85	| 6 | `AND` | left |
86	| 7 | `OR` | left |
87	
88	### Types and values
89	
90	- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
91	- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
92	- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
94	- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
95	- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.
96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.
104	
105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.
108	
109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
123	
124	### Aggregates and grouping
125	
126	- A query is an aggregate query if it has `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or `ORDER BY`.
127	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; `COUNT(e)` counts non-NULL values (INTEGER). `SUM` of INTEGER is INTEGER, of REAL is REAL. `AVG` is REAL. `MIN`/`MAX` keep the argument type. All ignore NULLs. Over zero non-NULL values `COUNT` is `0`, others NULL. `SUM`/`AVG` need numeric arguments; only `COUNT` accepts `*`.
128	- Without `GROUP BY` the whole filtered input (after `WHERE`) forms a single group, even when empty; without `HAVING` the query yields exactly one row, and `HAVING` filters that group, yielding 0 or 1 row (1 row over empty input when `HAVING` is true, e.g. `HAVING COUNT(*) = 0`). With `GROUP BY`, empty input yields zero rows; groups appear in first-seen order unless ordered.
129	- In an aggregate query, every select, `HAVING` and `ORDER BY` expression must be built from aggregate calls, literals, and subexpressions structurally identical to a `GROUP BY` expression (same resolved columns, operators and literals). `*` is not allowed. Aggregates are not allowed in `WHERE`, `ON`, `GROUP BY`, or inside another aggregate.
130	
131	### ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT
132	
133	- An `ORDER BY` item that is a bare INTEGER literal is a 1-based output ordinal, counted after `*` expansion. A bare identifier equal to exactly one select-item alias (written with or without `AS`) refers to that output column (two such aliases: ambiguous column). Otherwise it is an expression over input rows (or groups).
134	- With `DISTINCT`, each `ORDER BY` item must be an ordinal, an alias, or structurally identical to a select expression.
135	- Sorting is stable; ties keep pre-sort order for both `ASC` and `DESC`. NULL sorts before every value (first in `ASC`, last in `DESC`).
136	- `LIMIT 0` yields no rows; `OFFSET` past the end yields no rows.
137	
138	### Evaluation order
139	
140	1. `FROM`/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled row for an unmatched left row.
141	2. `WHERE` per row. 3. Group keys and aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. `HAVING` per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. `ORDER BY` keys. 7. `DISTINCT` (first occurrence kept). 8. Sort. 9. `OFFSET`, then `LIMIT`.
142	
143	`AND` skips its right side when the left is false; `OR` when the left is true. Rows are processed in order within each step; the first failure is reported and no output is produced.
144	
145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.
167	
168	### CLI
169	
170	`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.
171	
172	### REPL
173	
174	- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
175	- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
176	- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
177	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
178	- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.
179	
180	### Exit codes (one-shot)
181	
182	| Code | Meaning |
183	|---|---|
184	| 0 | success |
185	| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
186	| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
187	| 3 | IOError |
188	
189	On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.
190	
191	## Error handling
192	
193	Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.
194	
195	Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.
196	
197	| Kind | Message templates | Position |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
200	| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
201	| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
202	| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
203	| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |
204	
205	`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.

207	## Acceptance criteria
208	
209	Fixture `emp.csv`: `id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`. Fixture `dept.csv`: `code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`.
210	
211	- **AC1** (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
212	- **AC2** (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
213	- **AC3** (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
214	- **AC4** (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
215	- **AC5** (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
216	- **AC6** (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann` (header from the CSV, not the query).
217	- **AC7** (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
218	- **AC8** (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.

8	- Empty buffer: `line.strip(' \t\r\n')`. If that is empty the line is ignored. If it starts with `.` it is a command. Otherwise the line starts the buffer. Non-empty buffer: every line is appended with `\n`. Execute when `buffer.rstrip(' \t\r\n').endswith(';')`.
9	- Commands: the stripped line is split on `[ \t]+` (re). Exact lower-case words with exact arity. `.quit`/`.exit` (no args) return 0. `.help` prints a fixed text ending in `\n`. `.tables` prints one name per line. `.schema NAME` prints `name TYPE` per line. `.format csv|table` switches the format. 10	- Errors (`_guarded`): `MiniSQLError` gives `str(err)`. 11	- EOF: a non-empty buffer is executed with the same handling, then the function returns 0 and prints nothing more. Note: a prompt precedes every read, so the read that hits EOF on a pending buffer comes after a `   ...> ` prompt (for example stdin `SELECT 1` gives `minisql>    ...> ` + table).
